comments: Can't source an official translation of what I assume to be Nanase's mind-reading power. adjudicated.jp: 「世界最強のサブミッション、マスヲホールド（婿固め）だ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "It is the World's Strongest Submission, The Trout Hold (son-in-law clampdown)."
comments: Best I can do is this: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sazae-san it's long running, likely to be widely understood in Japan, written by a person with Machiko in the name (see below for more Machiko), a character named マスオ Masuo appears, his name is explicitly trout-inspired, and is a son-in-law.

Now, the manga's gone on for like 30 years, the anime has well over 6000 (!!!!!!!!!!!!) half-hour episodes, most of which are unavailable anywhere due to the author's wishes, and though there's at least one certain and another possible reference to same, see CCC0039 and CCD2002, this might be all completely unrelated.

The only alternative joke I got is a really bad fat joke ("hold the mass" with a pun for trout in there), or the "increase in mass" above, which is equally awful. Tanaka says in the Materials Book interview that in the PS2/PSP versions this would be expanded on, but I still got nothing.

Anyway, the term means 'son-in-law consolidation', but also has the implication of 'pledge', so she's securing him as son-in-law via corruption. As holding a trout's hard, according to such reliable sources as random googling, then adapted so it fits both. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Trout Hold does not preserve Masuo as a familiar name, but it deliberately closes the earlier trout callback and retains son-in-law clampdown in parentheses. The solution is debatable and overdependent on annotation, yet it is not a confirmed failure to represent either mechanism.
adjudicated.remedy: A stronger solution would preserve the name, move name and son-in-law senses without relying on the gloss.
